newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - May 2.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on May 2:
LONDON - Britain's Labour Party, led by Tony Blair, surged back to power for the first time since 1979, unseating by an apparently crushing margin the once mighty Conservative Party.

WASHINGTON - After climbing steadily for more than two decades, sexual activity among American teenagers has declined, the first drop since the federal government began tracking the information in 1970.

WASHINGTON - In the 52 years since Franklin Roosevelt's death and Friday's dedication of the memorial in West Potomac Park, historians have argued fiercely over almost everything in America's past except the historical stature of President Roosevelt.
WASHINGTON - Last-minute disputes over tax cuts kept the White House and Republicans from closing an historic agreement to balance the budget by 2002.

WASHINGTON - Troops from Angola equipped with armoured vehicles and heavy artillery have joined Zairean rebel forces pushing steadily towards Kinshasa in what appears to be the final drive to unseat President Mobutu Sese Seko.

WASHINGTON - Virtually every day an easily recognisable figure with unruly gray hair reports to work at his political headquarters in Pale, capital of the Bosnian Serb ministate. U.S. officials say they have no doubt that Radovan Karadzic, an indicted war criminal, is effectively calling the shots.
